hook.text: For 2,000 years, mathematicians tried to build a square with a circle's area using only compass and straightedge.

buildup.text: This requires constructing √π. If π is the wrong kind of number, the construction is impossible.

discovery.text: In 1882, Lindemann proved π is transcendental—not the root of any polynomial with rational coefficients.

twist.text: Compass-and-straightedge can only construct algebraic numbers. Transcendental numbers are permanently out of reach.

climax.text: Centuries of failure weren't due to lack of cleverness. The task was provably, permanently impossible.

quiz.question: Why is squaring the circle impossible?
options: π is transcendental and cannot be constructed with compass and straightedge
